PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket

**Firing.** Never fire the same cell repeatedly. Firing cell 5 at the same target every single round produced only misses; the target obviously isn't sitting there and gains information about my habits. Each fire stage, I pick a fresh cell — vary position across the whole 1–9 range and never repeat my last shot at the same target. A hit is worth 4 points to me and costs the target 1, so the standing-order target is still my best shot; I just need to actually hunt.

**Hiding.** Vary my cell every round and avoid any cell I've used recently, since opposing boats (Gamma hit me twice by apparently predicting or luck) are shooting at me on a fixed rotation. Avoid cells adjacent to my last one; if a boat has missed me, do not assume my cell stays safe — move anyway.

**Escort claims — this is where I left the most points on the table.** Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, more than a single hit. I never once named an escort and finished with nothing from this channel. Next time: use the note stage to openly propose a standing escort pairing ("Echo will claim Foxtrot every round if Foxtrot claims Echo"), then actually file [salvage: <partner>] every round. If the partner reciprocates even once, that's 5 points; over six rounds it could be 30. Propose it in round 1, restate it every round, and commit to naming them even before they've confirmed — a unilateral claim costs nothing.

**Notes.** A note that says "no observations" is a wasted broadcast. Notes are my only coordination channel. Use them to (a) set up the escort pairing, (b) report my shot results truthfully, and (c) announce my hiding-cell intentions to no one — never signal my own position.

**Claims.** The claim must match the office's private result anyway — there is no choice. File it immediately with no deliberation; the real decisions are hide, fire, and salvage.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The +3 payoff is outweighed by the removal threat and it breaks any coordination. Ignore Harbor as a target entirely.

**Score arithmetic to remember.** Endgame: hits give +4/-1, mutual escort gives +5 each. Escort cooperation with one opponent is worth more than repeatedly trying and failing to hit them. Priority: lock in the escort deal first, then hunt for hits with varied cells.

**What clearly did not work:** static firing (cell 5 forever), static notes ("steady on station" x4), and filing [salvage: none] every round. All three habits together produced a negative score.

1.text:
**Playbook for the sonar picket game.**

- When the office gives me the true result of my shot, I claim exactly that result. There is no bluffing: the claim is forced to match the private result, so trying to claim a hit on a miss gains nothing and just reveals I misread the rules. Never do that again.

- When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I fire at that station. Deviating buys nothing unless I have a concrete reason (e.g., a payoff mechanism I can exploit, like Harbor's jettison).

- Do not fire on Harbor unless the jettison math clearly beats the expected hit payoff and I'm certain the "off the board" threat isn't enforced. With no evidence the threat is empty, treat Harbor as off-limits.

- Hiding: the enemy firing at me is following the same standing order, so their shot is deterministic in target but guesses in cell. I should hide in cells that don't cluster with my past hiding spots and avoid repeatedly reusing the same cell — repetition let Echo (and Gamma) pattern me. Vary between low and high cells across rounds rather than settling on one favorite.

- When I hit a target, their next hide is likely to change; when I miss, their next hide is likely to stay. Adjust my fire cell accordingly: hit → shift my next shot at them away from their known spot's neighborhood by more than one; miss → stay near the same cell.

- Escort claims are pure coordination: 5 points each for mutual naming. I should establish a standing arrangement with one specific other boat via my station note early (e.g., "Foxtrot escorts Echo, Echo escort Foxtrot"), then name that boat every round. Leaving it at "none" every round forfeited 30 possible points across the patrol — that was my biggest missed source of score.

- Use the note stage to communicate, not to say "steady on station." Notes are relayed publicly to everyone; a repeated generic note is a wasted channel. Propose escort pairings and state my firing intent so others can coordinate.

- Track the score table at each hide stage. If I'm behind going into the last round, take the higher-variance action (spread shots to new cells); if ahead, play to avoid losing points — remember hits cost the target points too, so suppressing the leader matters.

- Final score came entirely from one lucky hit (4 points) plus nothing else. The reliable income in this game is the escort pairing — secure it first, treat hits as a bonus.

2.text:
**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

- Hiding: never reuse the same cell round after round. I hid in 7 repeatedly and got hit by Foxtrot in round 3. Alternate cells unpredictably, biased away from wherever I was last hit and away from "obvious" middling cells like 5.

- Firing: the standing order (fire at the next live station) is safe and scored me points — keep following it. But vary my fire cell; I fired at cell 5 every single round and hit only twice against a shifting target. Track which cells I've fired and where the target has been hit before, and pick untried cells. Never fire at Harbor — the 3-point jettison is not worth the threat of being put off the board.

- Claims: always claim the true result. The office forces the claim to match the private truth anyway (or close to it), so lying buys nothing and destroys credibility. Truthful reporting cost me nothing all game.

- Notes: keep them bland ("steady on station"). Revealing anything about my hide cell or intentions only helps opponents aim. Do not respond to probing notes with information.

- Escort: this was my biggest leak — I claimed "none" every round and left 5 points per round on the table. Mutual escort claims pay each of us 5 points, which dwarfs the 4 points from a hit. From round 1, propose an escort pact in notes ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot this round — Foxtrot, return the favor") and then name that boat every round. If I'm one of the shooting boats, the boat I'm NOT firing at is the natural escort partner — with standing-order fire there's no conflict between shooting one neighbor and escorting the other. Keep naming the same partner even if the pact is silent at first; worst case I lose nothing.

- If a round summary shows an opponent consistently targeting me, that's the boat to try to flip into an escort pact — a mutual 5-point payment is a better answer than hiding better.

- Endgame: nothing changes in the final round — keep the escort claim live (it's the largest single payout) and keep firing per standing order.
